title: Backdoor Trigger Detection via Mechanistic Alignment Analysis in Safety-Trained LLMs
summary: This paper introduces mechanistic alignment analysis to detect hidden backdoors in safety-trained LLMs by identifying neuron-level correlations between trigger conditions and unsafe outputs. The method combines activation clustering with counterfactual probing to expose discrepancies indicative of deceptive alignment failures, addressing gaps in behavioral safety evaluations.
gap: Ref-008 shows adversarial training fails to remove backdoors, creating false safety impressions. However, no work identifies neuron-level mechanisms enabling backdoor persistence despite safety training. Existing methods (ref-008, ref-019) detect behavioral failures but cannot isolate mechanistic causes of undetected backdoors.
approach: We implement mechanistic alignment analysis by: (1) training a classifier on neuron activations from backdoored models (ref-008) to detect trigger-response correlations, (2) applying counterfactual probing by masking identified neurons to test output consistency under hypothetical triggers, and (3) comparing results against adversarial training baselines (ref-008) and red-teaming methods (ref-019). The core model architecture and training data remain unchanged from ref-008's backdoored models.
evaluation: Evaluated on ref-008's year-triggered backdoor models (2023 vs. 2024 secure code generation). Compared against ref-008's adversarial training detection attempts and ref-019's red-teaming baselines. Measures: trigger detection rate (percentage of backdoored prompts correctly identified), false positive rate (safe prompts misclassified as backdoored), and alignment discrepancy score (difference in neuron activation patterns between triggered and non-triggered states). Ablation tests counterfactual probing by disabling neuron masking to isolate clustering's contribution.
